summary: Improve construction cost control, forecasting, and project reporting with practical exercises. Explore the five-day course and review the outline.
lede: Construction finance training helps project accountants, cost controllers, quantity surveyors, and commercial managers connect project activity with financial results. It covers job-cost and commitment analysis, earned value management, cost-to-complete forecasting, and project cash-flow planning. Participants practise using project records to explain forecast changes and support financial decisions.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who prepare, review, or act on construction project financial data, from job-cost entries through portfolio reporting. This course is designed for: Construction project accountants reconciling job costs, subcontractor invoices, and accruals. Construction cost controllers tracking budgets, commitments, and cost-to-complete forecasts. Quantity surveyors assessing valuations, variations, and project margin movement. Commercial managers reviewing contract changes, claims exposure, and cash flow. Construction finance managers consolidating project results and working-capital forecasts. Project controls analysts comparing planned progress with actual cost using earned value metrics. Site administrators coding purchase orders and verifying project cost documentation. Construction procurement managers monitoring subcontractor commitments and payment schedules. Construction operations directors reviewing project financial performance and forecast exceptions. Internal auditors testing construction cost controls, approvals, and project reporting evidence.
modules: Project Reporting and Financial Action Plans
prerequisites: Recommended: working familiarity with construction project budgets, job-cost reports, or project commercial records. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel access for spreadsheet-based exercises; no specialist software is required.
